summary.intent: Find out whether the 0.10.1 release succeeded or failed, and if it failed, diagnose the cause and fix it.
summary.outcome: The Release run failed at attestation verification and nothing was published (no 0.10.1 tags, crates.io still at 0.10.0). A fix was committed in a worktree: gh keeps its token, and the harness now enforces a token. A second commit fixes a flaky broken-pipe test, and the full `just ci` was rerun. The PR, the merge, and the recovery dispatch are still pending.

repo: The CLI runner scrubs release credentials from every child process except those a given program needs. Programs not on the allowlist, such as gh, lose GH_TOKEN, so `gh attestation verify` fails and Callisto reports it as E140.
The per-program credential scrubbing came from commit 660bae688 (the CLI layer of #177). The 0.10.0 tag predates it.

The release e2e harness used a fake gh that never required a token, so tests could not catch a missing GH_TOKEN. The harness now supplies a token and the fake gh refuses to run without one. With the old runner, 8 of 36 release e2e tests fail.

`just ci` runs tests under nextest and then re-runs them with plain `cargo test` in the coverage step. A test can pass under nextest and fail under cargo test, for example a broken-pipe test in output.rs. A nonzero exit (101) can therefore come from a later step even when all 1,896 tests pass.

Recovery for a failed release whose version commit is already on main is a `workflow_dispatch` of the release workflow with the explicit source SHA (6116efbd4). Merging the fix PR alone will not publish.
Changes need a changeset file in .changeset/.

code.finding: Credential scrubbing lives here. The fix allows GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN for gh, and a program given by path (such as /usr/bin/gh) is treated the same as its bare name. Exact line numbers were not given in the transcript.
A broken-pipe test was flaky under plain `cargo test`, and a fix was committed. Exact lines were not given in the transcript.

workflow: Verify a fix by reverting to the old code and confirming the new guard fails, then restore the fix. This showed the harness change catches the original bug.
Check `exit=` codes and the CI log rather than assuming a clean test count means a pass, because later steps can fail.
Rerun a suspect failing test alone several times to separate flakiness from regressions before blaming a change.
Do the fix in a worktree. Hold off on actions that publish, such as dispatching a release to crates.io, until the user gives an explicit go-ahead.

friction: The first Bash calls had to be repeated from the worktree and the worktree state checked before the release state could be read. This needed an ExitWorktree and a retry.
The previous testing missed the regression because every test used a fake gh that never needed a token.
`just ci` failed on a flaky broken-pipe test in the coverage step, which was unrelated to the fix and forced an extra commit and a CI rerun.
The release failed after merge, so 0.10.1 is not yet published even though main already carries the 0.10.1 versions.
open_items: Wait for the rerun of `just ci` to finish, then open the PR for the user to merge.
After the merge, dispatch the release workflow manually with source SHA 6116efbd4. This publishes to crates.io, so it needs the user's explicit approval first.
Confirm after the dispatch that the 0.10.1 tags and crates appear on all four crates.
